_note: sc-console-playwright manual-test-case convention. Combined suite for Event-Creation Notifications: Tray (PDT-3421 UC1 / PDT-3675, 5 AC) + Push (PDT-3420 UC1 console / PDT-3676, 3 AC + UC2 member / PDT-3677, 5 AC) = 13 AC. Direct-to-manual (no formal EC pipeline this pass), so covers[] is empty (manual-only) and acs[] carries the coverage guarantee — every one of the 13 AC appears in >=1 case. Console section expanded 3->8 from user's manual list (incl. message-template editor beyond PDT-3676 AC). Known bugs (BUG-B1/B2/C/D/E) are folded in as must-catch expectedResults. [ Backfill & old format ] REMOVED 2026-07-21: superseded by DEC-07 (release-date cutoff, user decision) — old events are excluded from this feature entirely, making the scenario untestable as an ongoing regression case once the cutoff ships. [ Backfill & old format ] RESTORED 2026-07-22: PM confirmed (TR-CL-30, answer C) old items DO get new copy — DEC-07's copy-exclusion clause was reversed.

sources.notes: Coverage guarantee via acs[] (13 AC). Tray runs on all 4 UIKit configs (iOS/Android/web-desktop/mobile-web); push receive/content/nav = iOS+Android only (web has no push); console = web-desktop. Derived from qa/PDT-3421 analysis + as-built source review (2026-07-16). Push-tap nav (PushMember AC-01/02) is host-app/integrator responsibility (P-CL-8) — shared destination nav also covered by Tray tap cases.

cases.name: [ Tray content ] Verify the event-created tray item shows community avatar, title, event-type chip, start date and time, and unseen state
cases.description: Core content of the enriched event-created tray item (5-element spec). Icon = community avatar (not user avatar / not event thumbnail).
cases.preconditions:
A community exists with an avatar set
The signed-in user is an active, non-banned member of that community
The Notification Tray is open on the target device
steps: Have a moderator create a new event in the community
Open the Notification Tray on the recipient device
Locate the newly created event item
expectedResults: The item icon is the COMMUNITY avatar (not the creator/user avatar and not an event thumbnail)
The primary line reads "[Community name] has event [Event name]"
The secondary line shows an event-type chip followed by the event start date and start time
The item is marked as unseen (unseen / primary-tint indicator)

cases.name: [ Tray content — deleted event ] Verify the tray item keeps the COMMUNITY avatar after its event is deleted
cases.description: Sibling of [ Tray content ] — same 5-element spec, but exercised AFTER the event is deleted (isDeleted = true). BUG-I: on web-desktop & mobile-web the item icon swaps to a DIFFERENT avatar once the event is deleted (no longer the community avatar). Distinct from [ Deleted event ] (Navigation), which checks the tap destination, not how the item itself renders.
cases.preconditions:
An event-created tray item is visible and correctly shows the COMMUNITY avatar
The signed-in user is an active, non-banned member of that community
A moderator can delete the event
steps: Confirm the fresh event item shows the community avatar as its icon
Have a moderator delete the event (isDeleted = true)
Refresh / re-open the Notification Tray
Re-locate the same event item and inspect its icon
expectedResults: The item icon is STILL the COMMUNITY avatar — identical to before the deletion
The icon is NOT swapped to the creator/user avatar, the event thumbnail, or any other image
The rest of the item content (title, chip, date/time) remains as specified
Known risk (BUG-I, web-desktop & mobile-web): after deletion the item shows a DIFFERENT avatar — that swap must FAIL this case

cases.name: [ Event type chip ] Verify the In-person and Virtual chips show the correct label and stay legible in light and dark theme
cases.description: TR-CL-21 / DEC-05 (expected = legible in both themes, per-platform divergence accepted) + BUG-D (Android chip white-on-white in LIGHT theme). Virtual == livestream (no third chip state).
cases.preconditions:
A test community is available for creating both In-person and Virtual (livestream) events
The target device/app supports both light and dark theme
steps: Create an In-person event and open its tray item
Create a Virtual / livestream event and open its tray item
View each item in LIGHT theme
View each item in DARK theme
expectedResults: The In-person event shows a chip labelled "In-person"
The Virtual / livestream event shows a chip labelled "Virtual" (there is no third chip type)
The chip text is legible (sufficient contrast) in LIGHT theme on every platform
The chip text is legible in DARK theme on every platform
Known risk (BUG-D): on Android the chip may render white-on-white in light theme — this must FAIL the legibility check

cases.name: [ Start time timezone ] Verify the tray date and time render in the viewer's local timezone (matching event cards and event detail)
cases.description: TR-CL-05 REVERSED 2026-07-21 (PM, after dev input): the tray follows existing UIKit behavior and shows the start time in the VIEWER's LOCAL timezone — same as event cards / event detail pages — NOT the event's own timezone. BUG-B1 is therefore RETRACTED: device-local is the intended behavior.
cases.preconditions:
Create an event and, in the timezone picker (shown as a GMT offset), select GMT-5 (e.g. New York / Eastern); set the start time to 7:00 PM on 10 Jul 2026
Set the viewer's device timezone to GMT+7 (e.g. Bangkok)
steps: Create the GMT-5 event as described
On the GMT+7 device, open the event-created tray item
Compare with the same event's start time on the event card / event detail page
expectedResults: The tray shows the start time converted to the VIEWER's local (GMT+7) timezone — i.e. 7:00 AM on 11 Jul 2026
This matches how the same event's start time is shown on the event card and the event detail page (all viewer-local)
It does NOT show the event's source-timezone wall-clock (must NOT show 7:00 PM on 10 Jul)

cases.name: [ Timestamp & separator ] Verify the relative notification timestamp renders and the date/time has no middle-dot separator
cases.description: TR-CL-19 (relative timestamp is tray chrome) + TR-CL-18 (no '·' separator — the PRD copy with a dot is wrong).
cases.preconditions: An event-created tray item is visible
steps: Observe the item's notification timestamp (corner / top)
Observe the secondary line between the date and the time
expectedResults: A relative timestamp is shown (e.g. Just now / 2m / 10h / a date)
There is NO '·' middle-dot separator between the date and the time
Date and time are separated by spacing only (per current design, not the PRD copy)

cases.name: [ Avatar fallback & truncation ] Verify the community-avatar fallback and long-name handling per platform
cases.description: TR-CL-15. Per-platform truncation differs and is accepted (Web/iOS wrap; Android ellipsizes ~3 lines).
cases.preconditions:
A community with NO avatar set
A community and event with very long names
steps: Trigger a tray item for the community that has no avatar
Trigger a tray item with very long community and event names
expectedResults: The no-avatar community shows a fallback (Web = community glyph, iOS = initials, Android = placeholder) — never a broken/empty icon
Long names do not break the layout or overlap other elements
Truncation may differ per platform (Web/iOS wrap; Android ellipsizes ~3 lines) — accepted as long as readable

cases.name: [ Public audience ] Verify a public-community event notifies the entire network including non-members, with no duplicate item
cases.description: AC-04 network-wide incl non-members (DEC-03) + TR-CL-14 dedup (UNION → 1 item). Needs >=3 accounts.
cases.preconditions:
A PUBLIC community
Account A = active member of that community
Account B = active network user who is NOT a member of that community
Account C = the event creator
steps: As Account C, create an event in the public community
Open the tray on Account A (member)
Open the tray on Account B (non-member network user)
Check Account A for duplicate items
expectedResults: Account A (member) receives ONE event-created tray item
Account B (non-member network user) ALSO receives the item, with the same content (community name shown even though B is not a member)
Account A sees only ONE item (a member who is also in the network is de-duplicated, not shown twice)
The creator (Account C) does NOT receive an item for their own event

cases.name: [ Private audience ] Verify a private-community event notifies only active, non-banned members
cases.description: AC-05. Private = members-only; non-members and banned members excluded.
cases.preconditions:
A PRIVATE community
Account A = active member
Account B = network user who is NOT a member
Account D = a member who is community-banned
steps: Create an event in the private community
Open the tray on Account A (member)
Open the tray on Account B (non-member)
Open the tray on Account D (banned member)
expectedResults: Account A (active member) receives the item
Account B (non-member) does NOT receive the item
Account D (banned member) does NOT receive the item
The creator does not receive their own item

cases.name: [ Exclusions ] Verify creator, banned, and blocked users are excluded at send and hidden at read
cases.description: TR-CL-08 creator + TR-CL-17 ban/leave after receive (hide at read, node kept) + TR-CL-24 user-block bidirectional.
cases.preconditions:
An event created in a community
A recipient who will be banned after receiving
A recipient who has a block relationship with the creator (either direction)
steps: Create the event and confirm eligible members received the item
Ban a recipient (global or community) and re-open their tray
Set up a block between a recipient and the creator, then create another event
expectedResults: The creator never receives their own event item
A user banned AFTER receiving no longer sees the item on next read (hidden at read; node not deleted)
Un-banning / re-joining within retention restores visibility
If the recipient and creator have a block relationship (either direction), the item is suppressed

cases.name: [ Block after notify ] Verify blocking after a notification was delivered blocks the recipient's access on tap
cases.description: TR-CL-29 Scenario A / DEC-08 (new scope, blocking extended to events, bidirectional). Different timing than [ Exclusions ], which covers a block made BEFORE the event is created.
cases.preconditions:
User A and User B are not blocked
User A creates an event in a shared community and User B receives the event-created tray item
User A then blocks User B (or User B blocks User A)
steps: As User B, open the Notification Tray
Tap the event's tray item that was received before the block
expectedResults: User B lands on a no-access state, even though the notification was delivered before the block existed

cases.name: [ Late join ] Verify a user who joins a private community after an event is created does not receive that event's notification
cases.description: TR-CL-23 — private community gives no retroactive backfill to a user who joins after the event was created.
cases.preconditions:
A PRIVATE community already has an event, and its event-created tray item was delivered to the members who were in the community at that time
A separate test user is NOT yet a member of that community
steps: Have the test user join the private community (after the event was created)
Open that user's Notification Tray
expectedResults: The newly joined user does NOT receive the earlier event's tray item
Only members who were in the community when the event was created received it (no retroactive backfill)

cases.name: [ Privacy change ] Verify switching a community to private keeps notifications already sent and guards access on tap
cases.description: TR-CL-16 / FU-4 — audience is a send-time snapshot (no recompute on privacy change); public->private exposure is handled by the nav/permission guard (event getById returns 403 for a non-member).
cases.preconditions:
A PUBLIC community created an event, so its tray item was delivered network-wide (including to non-members)
A non-member who received that item is signed in on the target device
steps: Switch the community from public to private
Open the non-member's Notification Tray
As that non-member, tap the event's tray item
expectedResults: The already-delivered tray item is NOT removed after the privacy change (audience is a snapshot at send time)
Tapping the now-private event is blocked — the event shows as unavailable and the non-member is not let in

cases.name: [ Tray tap ] Verify tapping an event-created tray item opens the event detail page with RSVP visible
cases.description: TR-CL-01 / FU-1. Destination = event detail page (RSVP CTA already visible there), not a separate RSVP page. Push reuses this same nav.
cases.preconditions: An event-created tray item is visible and the event still exists
steps: Tap the event-created tray item
expectedResults: The event detail page opens
The RSVP action / button is visible on that page
This is the shared destination that a push tap also routes to once wired

cases.name: [ Deleted event ] Verify tapping a tray item for a deleted event shows a graceful unavailable state with no crash or blank
cases.description: TR-CL-03 + BUG-C (Android shows 'This community is private' for a DELETED event) + BUG-E (web FailedToShow flash on load). iOS conflates deleted vs forbidden.
cases.preconditions: An event-created tray item whose event is then deleted (isDeleted = true) before tapping
steps: Delete the event
Tap the tray item for the deleted event
expectedResults: A graceful 'no longer available' state is shown — no crash, no error, no blank screen
A Go-back / dismiss path is available
Known risk (BUG-C, Android): a deleted event must NOT say 'This community is private' — that wrong message must FAIL
Known risk (BUG-E, web): the unavailable screen must not flash before the content finishes loading

cases.name: [ Left community ] Verify a former member tapping the event notification after leaving sees it as no longer available
cases.description: TR-CL-27. Same nav-guard family as [ Privacy change ], triggered by the member leaving rather than a privacy flip.
cases.preconditions:
A member of a PRIVATE community received an event-created tray item
That member then leaves the private community
steps: As the former member, open the Notification Tray or the original notification
Tap the event's tray item
expectedResults: The event shows as no longer available
The former member is not let into the private community's event

cases.name: [ Event ended ] Verify tapping a notification for an ended event opens Event Detail with no RSVP button
cases.description: TR-CL-28. Contrast with [ Deleted event ]: an ended event still exists and opens normally, it just no longer offers RSVP — it does NOT show an 'unavailable' state.
cases.preconditions: An event-created tray item exists for an event whose scheduled time has already passed (the event has ended)
steps: Tap the event's tray item
expectedResults: The Event Detail page opens (not an 'unavailable' state)
The page shows an ended state
No RSVP button is shown

cases.name: [ No grouping ] Verify each event creation produces its own distinct tray item
cases.description: TR-CL-04 — no grouping, even for multiple events from the same community.
cases.preconditions: One community that will host multiple events
steps: Create 3 events in the same community
Open the tray
expectedResults: Each event appears as its OWN separate tray item
Items are NOT grouped or collapsed even when they come from the same community

cases.name: [ Unseen & seen ] Verify the unseen indicator is computed correctly and clears only on mark-seen, not on fetch
cases.description: AC-01 unseen + TR-CL-06 (client computes lastTrayOccurredAt > lastTraySeenAt; seen set by markTraySeen/markItemsSeen only; fetch does not set seen).
cases.preconditions: A fresh event-created tray item that has never been seen
steps: Fetch / load the tray list without triggering the mark-seen action
Trigger the seen action (open tray / mark seen per platform)
Re-open the tray
expectedResults: A new item appears as unseen
Merely fetching the list does not by itself flip the item to seen if mark-seen is not triggered
After mark-seen, the item shows as seen and the unseen count decreases

cases.name: [ Event edited ] Verify editing an event updates its existing tray item (live, not a snapshot)
cases.description: TR-CL-12 — serializer re-fetches the event at read; edit reflects after the short Redis cache TTL.
cases.preconditions: An event-created tray item exists
steps: Edit the event's name / time / type
Wait for the cache TTL to expire
Re-open the tray item
expectedResults: The tray item reflects the UPDATED event details (name / time / type)
It is not frozen to the values at creation time (live re-fetch, not a snapshot)

cases.name: [ Backfill & old format ] Verify pre-existing items get the new content at read and network broadcast stays forward-only
cases.description: TR-CL-13, CONFIRMED by PM via TR-CL-30 (2026-07-22, answer C): an old event (created before this release) shows the new rich content when reopened, but does not newly start reaching the whole network.
cases.preconditions:
An event exists that was created before this release, in a community (its tray item still shows the old content, e.g. "You've been invited to an event")
A second test account is a network user who is NOT a member of that community
steps: As a member of that community, open the old event's tray item
As the second account (non-member of that community), check whether the same tray item appears
expectedResults: The member sees the old item now showing the new content (community avatar, chip, start date, start time) — not the old generic text
The non-member does NOT see that item — it has not started reaching the whole network

cases.name: [ Console toggle ] Verify the event-creation push toggle is present and correctly labelled
cases.description: PDT-3676 AC-01. Toggle = event-activate-switch (field isPushNotifiable) under the 'Event-related events' section.
cases.preconditions:
The signed-in account is a network admin with Admin Console access
Push notifications are enabled for the network
steps: Open Admin Console → Settings → Push notifications
Open the Community tab / 'Event-related events' section
expectedResults: A section titled 'Event-related events' is present
It contains a toggle labelled 'When someone creates a new event in the community'
The toggle sits alongside the 'event reminder' and 'event started' toggles

cases.name: [ Toggle on ] Verify enabling the toggle sends a push to community members and deep-links to the event
cases.description: PDT-3676 AC-03 + P-CL-2 (members only, not network-wide). Combines list #1 (enable) with delivery.
cases.preconditions:
The 'When someone creates a new event in the community' toggle is OFF
Account A is an active, non-banned member of the community (push enabled)
Account B is a network user who is not a member of the community (push enabled)
steps: Turn the toggle ON and save
Create a new event in a PUBLIC community as another user
Observe the push on Account A (member)
Observe the push on Account B (non-member)
expectedResults: The toggle switches to ON and the setting persists
Account A (member) receives an event-creation push
Account B (non-member) does NOT receive the push — audience is community members only, even for a public community (unlike the tray)
Tapping the push deep-links to the event (once push-tap is wired in the host app)

cases.name: [ Toggle off ] Verify disabling the toggle stops the push while the in-app tray still fires
cases.description: PDT-3676 AC-02 + list #2. Cross-surface: push and tray are independent.
cases.preconditions:
The 'When someone creates a new event in the community' toggle is ON
A member device with push enabled
steps: Turn the toggle OFF and save
Create a new event in the community
Observe the member device for a push
Open the member's in-app notification tray
expectedResults: The toggle switches to OFF and the setting persists
No event-creation push is delivered
The in-app tray item still appears to community members (the tray is independent of the push toggle)

cases.name: [ Edit message ] Verify the push message template can be edited, placeholders inserted, and saved
cases.description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC — the console 'Edit message for event' modal (Notification Title + Notification Text + placeholder buttons). Merges list #3, #4, #5, #6.
cases.preconditions:
The signed-in account can edit push-notification settings
The 'Event-related events' list is visible
steps: Click the edit (pencil) icon in the Actions column for the event-creation row
Replace the Notification Title with e.g. 'New event in {{CommunityName}}!'
Replace the Notification Text with e.g. '{{EventName}} starts on {{EventStartDate}}'
Place the cursor in a field and click a placeholder button e.g. {{EventType}}
Click OK / Save
expectedResults: The 'Edit message for event' modal opens showing the current Notification Title, Notification Text, and the list of supported placeholders
Clicking a placeholder button inserts that placeholder at the cursor position
On save, the edited title and text persist
A newly created event's push reflects the edited title and body, with placeholders replaced by real values

cases.name: [ Message validation ] Verify the title and text length limits and empty-field handling
cases.description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. Title limit 62, Text limit 235, empty-field block. Merges list #7, #8, #9.
cases.preconditions: The 'Edit message for event' modal is open
steps: Type more than 62 characters in the Notification Title field
Type more than 235 characters in the Notification Text field
Clear the Title and/or Text field to leave it empty
Click OK / Save
expectedResults: The Title field does not accept more than 62 characters; its counter (x/62) updates correctly
The Text field does not accept more than 235 characters; its counter (x/235) updates correctly
An empty Title or Text shows a validation error and is not saved

cases.name: [ Modal controls ] Verify Restore Default reverts and Cancel or X discards changes
cases.description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. Merges list #10, #11, #12.
cases.preconditions: The 'Edit message for event' modal is open with the title/text edited but not yet saved
steps: Click 'Restore Default'
Edit the fields again, then click 'Cancel'
Reopen the modal, edit the fields, then click the X (top-right)
expectedResults: 'Restore Default' reverts the Notification Title and Text to the system's original default values
'Cancel' closes the modal without saving — reopening shows the pre-edit text
The X button closes the modal without saving

cases.name: [ Template rendering ] Verify saved placeholders and emoji render as real values in the delivered push
cases.description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. Merges list #13, #14 — verifies the console edit produces correct push output.
cases.preconditions:
The push message template is edited to include all placeholders and an emoji / special characters, and saved
The toggle is ON
A member device (iOS / Android) with push enabled
steps: Create an event named 'Yoga Night' in the community 'Fitness Club', type virtual, starting 21 Jul 2026 18:00
Observe the delivered push on the member device
expectedResults: The push replaces {{CommunityName}} with 'Fitness Club', {{EventName}} with 'Yoga Night', and fills {{EventType}}, {{EventStartDate}}, {{EventStartTime}} with the real event values
Emoji and special characters display correctly with no encoding issues
The start date/time render in the viewer's device-local timezone (consistent with the tray; verified on Android + iOS)

cases.name: [ Access control ] Verify push-notification settings are restricted by role
cases.description: Beyond PDT-3676 AC. List #16.
cases.preconditions: The signed-in account has a role that lacks access to the push-notification settings
steps: Attempt to open the Push notifications settings page
Attempt to edit the event-creation toggle or message
expectedResults: Access is denied or a permission-denied message is shown, per the role's permissions
An unauthorized role cannot change the setting or the message

cases.name: [ Push content ] Verify the push shows the correct title, body chip and date/time, and community-avatar icon
cases.description: PDT-3677 AC-05. OS notification text is server-rendered. Icon = community avatar.
cases.preconditions:
The event-creation push toggle is ON
A member device (iOS / Android) with push enabled
steps: Create an In-person event in the community
Observe the push notification on the member device
Repeat with a Virtual event
expectedResults: The push title reads '[Community name] has event [Event name]'
The push body shows the event-type chip label ('In-person' or 'Virtual') followed by the start date and start time
The notification icon is the community avatar
An event with an unknown type shows an empty chip label ('')

cases.name: [ Push timezone ] Verify the push start time renders in the viewer's device-local timezone (matching the tray)
cases.description: Push shows the start time in the VIEWER's device-local timezone — consistent with the tray (DEC-06) and existing UIKit surfaces. VERIFIED CORRECT on Android + iOS (2026-07-21). Supersedes BUG-B2: the earlier source-based 'push renders UTC' inference did not reproduce on device.
cases.preconditions:
Create an event and, in the timezone picker (shown as a GMT offset), select GMT-5 (e.g. New York / Eastern); set the start time to 7:00 PM on 10 Jul 2026
Set the viewer's device timezone to GMT+7 (e.g. Bangkok)
The event-creation push toggle is ON
steps: Create the GMT-5 event with the push toggle ON
On the GMT+7 device, observe the push notification body
expectedResults: The push body shows the start time converted to the viewer's device-local (GMT+7) timezone — i.e. 7:00 AM on 11 Jul 2026
It matches the in-app tray and event detail (all viewer-local)
It does NOT show raw UTC (12:00 AM / midnight 11 Jul) nor the event's source-tz wall-clock (7:00 PM 10 Jul)

cases.name: [ Virtual single push ] Verify a virtual event delivers exactly one push with the Room go-live push suppressed
cases.description: PDT-3677 AC-04. Dedup is backend-only; no client-side dedup exists.
cases.preconditions:
The push toggle is ON
A member device with push enabled
steps: Create a VIRTUAL event (which auto-generates a Room)
Observe all push notifications delivered to the member device
expectedResults: Exactly ONE push notification is delivered for the event
No separate Room / livestream-creation push arrives for the same event (it is suppressed)

cases.name: [ OS opt-out ] Verify a device or OS push opt-out stops the push but not the in-app tray
cases.description: PDT-3677 AC-03. push and tray are independent.
cases.preconditions:
A member has disabled push for the app at the device / OS level
The push toggle is ON at network level
steps: Disable push for the app in device / OS settings
Create an event in the community
Observe the device for a push
Open the in-app notification tray
expectedResults: No push is delivered (the OS suppresses it)
The in-app tray item still appears (the tray is independent of the OS push opt-out)

cases.name: [ Push tap ] Verify tapping the push opens the event detail / RSVP page
cases.description: PDT-3677 AC-01 + P-CL-8: push-tap routing is host-app/integrator responsibility (not wired in the reference sample apps). Destination nav is the SAME as the tray tap. Run on a push-integrated host build.
cases.preconditions:
A push-integrated host app that routes the event.created payload (eventId) to the UIKit event detail page
An event-creation push has been received
steps: Tap the received event-creation push
expectedResults: The event detail / RSVP page for that event opens (routed off the eventId payload)
The RSVP action is visible
If the host app does not wire push-tap routing, this cannot be verified on that build — the shared destination nav is covered by the Tray tap case

cases.name: [ Push deleted ] Verify tapping a push for a deleted event shows a graceful unavailable state
cases.description: PDT-3677 AC-02 + shared BUG-C (Android). Same nav path as the Tray deleted-event case; event getById returns 404.
cases.preconditions:
A push-integrated host build
An event-creation push whose event is deleted before tapping
steps: Delete the event after the push is delivered
Tap the push
expectedResults: A graceful 'This event is no longer available' state is shown (event getById returns 404)
No error or blank screen
Known risk (BUG-C, Android): must NOT show 'This community is private' for a deleted event

cases.name: [ Block hides event in Hub ] Verify blocked users don't see each other's events in the Event Hub
cases.description: TR-CL-29 Scenario C / DEC-08 (new scope). Cross-surface check: validates the same block rule Jack is adding, on the Event Hub / Event tab listing rather than the notification tray.
cases.preconditions:
User A and User B are both members of the same community
User A and User B have a block relationship (either direction)
steps: As User A, create an event in the shared community
As User B, open the Event tab / Event Hub for that community
As User A, open the Event tab / Event Hub and look for any event User B created
expectedResults: User B does not see User A's event in the Event tab / Event Hub
User A does not see User B's events either — hidden from each other both ways
